mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which correlates with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.1%, it signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equities and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.1% occurs in 10 consecutive months without producing positive 5-day returns in at least 7 of them.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a coordinated monetary and labor market stimulus, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing and labor market improvement
failure_condition: The correlation between the joint FEDFUNDS decline and UNRATE decline with 60-day SPX returns falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In housing boom regimes (HOUST > 900 thousand units), strong residential construction activity drives consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST above 900 occurs in 15 consecutive months with negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth in a month fails to produce positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL 12m change) exceeds 2.5%, it triggers expectations of monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL 12m change above 2.5% occurs in 12 consecutive months without negative 60-day SPX returns in at least 8 of them.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer spending and labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint RSAFS and PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 8.0%), economic weakness and reduced consumer spending lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE above 8.0% occurs in 10 consecutive months with negative 5-day SPX returns in less than 60% of cases.
